bodies.linkedin:
A single factual error by an AI chatbot once contributed to a $100 billion decline in a company's market value.

Retrieval-augmented generation is one method explored to help models stick to facts by blending their processing with external document or web lookups. This approach can help mitigate AI hallucinations, such as the invention of nonexistent policies or legal citations.

Even with these methods, models may still produce misinformation if they fail to interpret the context of retrieved information correctly. It is not a direct solution because the LLM can still hallucinate around the source material in its response.

Developers are also using these techniques to reduce the financial and computational requirements associated with retraining models on new data. In some cases, redesigning a language model with a retriever allows a network that is 25-time smaller to reach comparable perplexity to larger models.

Retrieval-augmented generation does not entirely remove the need for frequent model retraining.

Developers use this to avoid the high costs of retraining models whenever new data becomes available.
